sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Majority Ownership**: Defined under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Acts of 1970 and 1980, requiring the Central Government to maintain at least **51% equity stake**.
• **Socio-Economic Mandate**: Unlike private banks driven purely by profit maximization, PSBs carry developmental obligations including **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** targets (40% of ANBC), rural branching, and financial inclusion.
• **Monetary Policy Transmission**: PSBs act as primary transmission channels for RBI's repo rate changes, though structural rigidities like high legacy NPAs often cause transmission lags.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) governed by **Basel III norms**, monitored closely by RBI through prompt corrective action (PCA) frameworks.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Largest public sector bank with global footprint, legacy of Imperial Bank of India (1955).
SBI Act, 1955; separated from associate banks via consolidation.
Frequently tested as a statutory corporation, not just a company under Companies Act.
14 banks nationalized in 1969 (deposits > ₹50 cr) and 6 in 1980 (deposits > ₹200 cr) by Indira Gandhi.
Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Acts.
Historical watershed moment shifting credit focus toward agriculture and small industries.
Post-2019 mega-mergers reduced PSBs from 27 to 12. Key anchors: PNB, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Union Bank.
Amalgamation schemes framed under Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
Mains evaluation topic: economies of scale vs. governance and regional credit dilution.

items.definition: A framework where the RBI puts banks with weak financial metrics (capital, asset quality, profitability) under supervisory watch, restricting branch expansion, dividend distribution, and risky lending.

items.term: Bad Bank (National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd - NARCL)
items.definition: An asset management company that takes over stressed assets (NPAs) from commercial banks to clean up their balance sheets, operating alongside IDRCL (India Debt Resolution Company Ltd).
A 7-pronged reform package launched in 2015 covering appointments (BBB), capitalization, de-stressing, empowerment, accountability, governance, and bad debt resolution.

Narasimham Committee I (1991) and II (1998) on banking reforms; P.J. Nayak Committee (2014) on Governance of Boards of Banks; Banking Regulation (Amendment) Act, 2020 extending RBI's powers over cooperative and public sector banks.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution & Rural Penetration
items.content:
• **Spatial Spread**: Mandated under RBI licensing conditions to maintain a specific proportion of branches in unbanked rural and semi-urban areas (Tier 5 and Tier 6 centres).
• **Regional Imbalances**: Historical concentration of credit-deposit (CD) ratios in metropolitan and urban industrial belts compared to aspirational districts.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Twin Balance Sheet (TBS) problem, legacy Non-Performing Assets (NPAs), cyber security vulnerabilities, and human resource/succession challenges at top management levels.
• **Policy Interventions**: Recapitalization bonds, establishment of National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID), PSB Manthan strategic roadmaps.

items.title: Mnemonic for 4 Anchor Banks Post-2020 Mega Merger
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'P'lease 'B'ring 'C'offee 'U'rgent (P, B, C, U)
• **Decoded Meaning**: Punjab National Bank (PNB), Bank of Baroda (BoB), Canara Bank, Union Bank of India.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly recalls the four primary anchor banks surviving the massive 2019-20 consolidation wave.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: 1969 Nationalization threshold = ₹50 Crore deposit base; 1980 Nationalization threshold = ₹200 Crore deposit base.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames statements like 'All Public Sector Banks in India are established under the Companies Act, 2013.' This is INCORRECT. While nationalized banks were formed via specific acquisition acts and SBI via the SBI Act, 1955, only some operate under the broader company law framework with government majority holding.

Mains Value Addition: Quote the Economic Survey's emphasis on balancing commercial viability with social objectives. Use keywords like 'Twin Balance Sheet stress', 'Professionalization of Bank Boards via Banks Board Bureau (now FSIB)', and 'Credit-Deposit Ratio optimization'.

keyTakeaways: PSBs maintain a government majority stake (>51%) and act as the principal instruments for priority sector lending and rural financial inclusion.
Historical evolution moved from the 1955 SBI nationalization and 1969/1980 waves to the 2020 mega-consolidation reducing PSBs to 12.
Key governance and asset quality frameworks like PCA, NARCL, and Basel III norms are vital for analyzing banking stability and UPSC objective questions.
